body: According to the opinion, C&B Development, LLC is the equitable owner, under an August 2022 purchase agreement, of a 75.5-acre tract in Maxatawny Township, Berks County, now improved with a restaurant, a mobile home park and an airport. The tract lies in three zoning districts, Commercial (C-1), Light Industrial (L-I) and Agricultural Preservation (AP-1), and has frontage only on Kutztown Road. The developer plans to demolish the existing uses and build a commercial building and a 709,000-square-foot warehouse on the L-I portion, which can be reached only by a new private road, Road A, through the commercial district.

An ordinance amendment effective October 13, 2022 made warehouses a conditional use in the L-I district and added Section 593(c), which requires warehouse buildings and "all related impervious surfaces" to be at least 500 feet from a building occupied by an existing residential, institutional or educational use. On August 31, 2023 the zoning officer determined that Road A was an impervious surface serving the warehouse that could not meet the setback, and that the developer needed a variance before its conditional use hearing could proceed.

The developer appealed to the Zoning Hearing Board and alternatively sought a dimensional variance. After hearings ending in January 2024, the Board on January 15, 2024 upheld the zoning officer and denied the variance, finding the property could be used for many permitted uses without the 500-foot buffer and that Road A would bring hundreds of tractor trailers onto Kutztown Road in a largely residential area used by Kutztown University students. The Berks County Court of Common Pleas affirmed on July 14, 2025.

In a memorandum opinion by Judge Patricia A. McCullough filed October 14, 2026, the Commonwealth Court affirmed. The zoning officer's absence from the hearings was no ground for reversal, because the Board interprets the ordinance itself and the developer withdrew its plan to subpoena him. The conditional use provision and the setback did not conflict, so the Municipalities Planning Code's rule resolving doubtful language in the owner's favor did not apply. And because the developer admitted the L-I land could be used for other purposes, its hardship was self-imposed rather than a function of the property. The court noted that the developer had not brought a formal challenge to the ordinance's validity, and it declined to consider material from the developer's separate, pending inverse condemnation suit against the township. The opinion is designated as not reported.

timeline.label: Ordinance amendment takes effect, making warehouses a conditional use subject to the Section 593(c) 500-foot buffer
C&B Development submits its conditional use plan
Zoning officer rules the access road is subject to the buffer and needs a variance
Zoning Hearing Board upholds the zoning officer and denies the variance
Berks County Court of Common Pleas affirms
